definitions.explanation: A stretched cord on a musical instrument such as a guitar, violin, or koto that produces sound when plucked or bowed.
The string of a bow used in archery.

examples.japanese: ⟦ギター→ギター：04461_gitaa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{弦|げん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{切|き}れた→切れる：01936_kireru⟧。
⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{弦|げん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{張|は}り{替|か}えた→張り替える：28418_harikaeru⟧。
examples.english: I replaced the strings with new ones.

examples.japanese: ⟦バイオリン→バイオリン：00009_baiorin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{四|よん}→四：00767_yon⟧{本|ほん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{弦|げん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{様々|さまざま}→様々：01559_samazama⟧な⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: A violin produces various sounds with four strings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{弓道|きゅうどう}→弓道：04453_kyuudou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{弦|げん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{張|は}り⟦{具合|ぐあい}→具合：01391_guai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ。
examples.english: In Japanese archery, the tension of the bowstring is important.
When the bowstring was released, the arrow flew away.

notes:
{弦|げん} can also be read as {弦|つる} with the same meanings. The reading {弦|げん} is more common in compounds and musical contexts, while {弦|つる} is used more in standalone or traditional contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弦|げん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}る→張る：12583_haru⟧ — to string (an instrument or bow)
- {弦|げん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{弾|ひ}く→弾く：02444_hiku⟧ — to pluck a string
- ⟦{弦|げん}{楽器|がっき}→弦楽器：07534_gengakki⟧ — stringed instrument
- ⟦{三味線|しゃみせん}→三味線：04464_shamisen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{弦|げん} — shamisen string

COUNTING: Strings are counted with {本|ほん} (⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧, {二本|にほん}...).
